_comment: ngsolve contact#6 (checking the displacement residual alone can return with the contact gap still violated). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: elastic block E=1000 nu=0.3 on maxh 0.2, fixed on top, body force 150 onto a floor 0.01 below, penalty contact through ngsolve.solvers.Newton at gamma=1e4. Newton returns status 0 in 3 iterations, and one further Newton step taken by hand from the converged state gives a relative increment of 7.8e-17 -- ten decades under the claim's 1e-6, so the displacement criterion is met with enormous margin. At that same state the claim's own expression, max over the boundary of min(gap,0) with gap = u_y+G0, is 5.96e-3, which is 2.98% of an element edge and sits inside the 1-5% band the claim names. The gap check fires there; the displacement check does not. Raising gamma to 1e7 clears the gap check (7.2e-6) while the displacement verdict is unchanged, so the gap check carries information the displacement check never had. Mutation: setting gamma to 1e7 for the first solve puts the gap under tolerance and the fixture fails on gap_violation_in_claimed_1_to_5_pct_band and displacement_ok_but_gap_violated.
